reason: Reduced is a size or degree word and ridged is a surface feature. They are not alternatives of one character, and 'reduced' looks like a wrong grounding of a reduction cue.
Simple or fascicled hairs are the usual trichome-type alternatives. Both groundings fit the example.
Spinulose or tomentose are alternative surface coverings in a flora. Both groundings fit. The example names two parts, sheath and petiole, but the 'or' joins the two coverings.
Erect or radiating are alternatives of orientation or posture, and the example is about one part.
Concave is a shape and spreading is an orientation. The example has no bearer, and the two words probably refer to different parts.
Adherent or loose bark are alternatives of how the bark attaches. Both groundings fit.
Striate or flaky are alternative bark surface textures.
Divaricate or verticillate are alternatives of the branching pattern, and the example says so.
Bony or coriaceous are alternatives of tissue texture or consistency.
Channelled or plicate are alternative longitudinal folding or grooving states of a blade or petiole.
Appressed is an orientation or attachment and umbonate is a shape. They are unrelated characters, and the example gives no context to link them.
Reticulate or papillose are alternative surface sculptures, for example of a seed or pollen wall.
'Extends beyond' is a wrong grounding. The example has only 'attenuate' and 'usually' and no second value.
Approximate or verticillate are alternatives of the arrangement of the parts, such as leaves or branches.
The example is only 'plane', and 'distributed' is a spurious grounding. This is not an alternative.
'Sub-sessile' is one word. 'Dendritic' is a spurious grounding and there is no alternative.
'Gradually thickened' describes the shape of the stigma, not the PATO thickness quality. Grounding it as increased thickness is wrong, so the pair is not accepted.
'Very slightly raised above' is a relation to a surface, qualified by degree. It is not an alternative of the same character as smooth.
The shape is cylindrical, and the contraction is a local, distal and occasional feature. They are not alternatives of one character.
Filiform or inflated are alternatives of the form of the rhachis, thin or swollen.
'Apiculate' is grounded to the generic 'sharpness' attribute, which is a wrong grounding. Capitate is a shape, so the pair fails the check.
Conduplicate or open are alternatives of how a leaf or other organ is folded.
'Short' is a length and 'stolon-like' is a form. They are different characters, and this is a combination of length and form.
Scabrous is a texture and serrulate is a margin shape. The pair is doubtful, so reject it.
The example is only 'slightly curved'. 'Asymmetrical' is a spurious grounding and there is no alternative.
Black or speckled seeds are alternatives of the seed colour or colour pattern, and both groundings fit.
'Distal' is a position and 'continuous' describes the wing. These are different characters, and 'distal to' is a spatial relation.
Wrinkled is a surface texture and flattened is a shape. The example is about one state, at base, when dry.
Tangled or tufted are alternative growth forms of the stems or the plant.
The example is only 'slightly concave'. 'Furrowed' is a spurious grounding and there is no alternative.
'Ternate' as leaf division is wrongly grounded to 'ternately compound'. 'Alternate placement' is an arrangement, so the pair mixes different characters.
'Densely branched' and 'compact from base' are two descriptions of the plant habit, not a plain alternative. The degree cues are part of both.
'Discolored' is a change of colour, not a colour value. It is a poor grounding for the pair.
Pitted or ribbed are alternative surface sculpture states. The 'somewhat' cue applies to both.
Male or mixed are alternatives of the sexual composition of the clusters (inflorescence).
The example is only 'anthers sterile'. 'Vestigial' is a spurious grounding and there is no alternative.
The example is only 'longitudinally striate'. 'Tuberculate' is a spurious grounding and there is no alternative.
'Glomeruliform' is wrongly grounded to 'aggregated', which is a spatial arrangement rather than the shape of the part. It does not match 'fusiform'.
Prostrate or cushion-shaped are alternatives of the growth habit of the dwarf shrub or herb.
Peltate is an attachment or insertion and clavate is a shape. The part is unspecified, which makes a wrong grounding likely. Reject as doubtful.
